# Diagnosing the Idle-Out Condition on a 1991 Cadillac STS

When you press the accelerator pedal to the floor on a 1991 Cadillac STS equipped with the 4.9L V8 and the engine immediately dies or refuses to pick up speed, you are facing a classic "no-load" scenario. The fact that there is no smoke from the tailpipes confirms the engine isn't mechanically seizing or flooding excessively with unburnt fuel, but it points directly to an inability to sustain combustion under load or maintain idle stability during transition.

The most common culprit in this specific configuration is not the fuel injectors themselves failing, but rather the fuel delivery system's inability to meet the sudden demand for pressure and volume. The 4.9L engine relies on a mechanical fuel pump located on the nose of the distributor. Under wide-open throttle (WOT) conditions, the pump must work significantly harder to push fuel through the rail. If the pump is worn, clogged with debris from old gasoline, or if the filter is restricted, the pressure drops instantly when the load increases. This causes a lean condition that the engine control module (ECM) cannot compensate for fast enough, resulting in the engine stalling or stumbling violently.

To verify this, you need to check the fuel pressure at the test port on the fuel rail while someone presses the gas pedal. If the needle drops from approximately 7-9 psi to near zero instantly, the mechanical pump is failing. Replacing a mechanical pump often involves removing the distributor cap and belt, which is straightforward but requires careful handling of the high-tension drive belts found on these GM V8s.

Another critical area to inspect is the intake air system. On vehicles of this era, vacuum leaks can mimic fuel starvation because they dilute the air-fuel mixture with extra unmetered air. When you floor it, the ECU tries to compensate by opening the throttle further and adjusting injectors, but a massive leak can overwhelm the correction algorithm, causing the engine to die. Common failure points include the PCV valve, the brake booster vacuum hose, or cracked intake manifold gaskets. Listen for a distinct hissing sound near the firewall or use a propane enrichment test (carefully introducing propane around suspected leaks while the engine is running) to see if RPMs increase temporarily, confirming an air leak.

The transmission is noted as good in your description, which eliminates slipping gears as a cause for the lack of acceleration. However, ensure that the torque converter lock-up solenoid isn't causing drag issues, though this usually presents differently than an immediate stall. If the engine cuts out completely at high RPMs, check the ignition system. Worn distributor points or failing ignition coils can cause misfires under load. The 1991 STS uses a dual coil pack design; if one side fails to fire consistently when demand spikes, the engine will lose power and may stall if it loses all cylinders simultaneously due to timing issues triggered by the load drop.

Before replacing expensive components like fuel injectors, rule out the mechanical delivery chain and vacuum integrity. The ECM can adjust for a slightly lean mixture, but it cannot create fuel where none exists or correct for a massive air leak instantly. If you have access to an OBD-I scanner (using the Data Link Connector under the dash), monitor the Short Fuel Trim values. Positive short-term fuel trim numbers indicating above +10% suggest the computer is already trying to add more fuel, meaning the system is maxed out or the injectors are clogged.

If the fuel pump and vacuum seals check out clean, consider the condition of the throttle body. Carbon buildup on the butterfly plate can prevent it from opening fully or smoothly, creating a restriction that feels like a lack of power. A thorough cleaning with a suitable carburetor/throttle body cleaner and a soft brush can restore proper airflow dynamics. Always clear the ECM codes after repairs to ensure the fuel trim values reset correctly, allowing the system to learn the new baseline without fighting old adaptive data.
